§6Bakelite§f

§aPlastic from oil fluids only  -  no coal, no fluorite, just aromatic hydrocarbons and petroleum gas!§f

Bakelite (formally polyoxybenzylmethyleneglycolanhydride) is a polymer substitute made from §bAromatic Hydrocarbons§f and §bPetroleum Gas§f in the §bChemical Plant§f. Recipe: §e500mB§f of each yields §e1×§f Bakelite Bar.

§6Why use it§f:
§b•§f Replaces Polymer in virtually every recipe.
§b•§f No coal powder or fluorite needed, just oil products.
§b•§f Far easier to mass-produce once your oil refinery is running.

§6Main use§f:
§b•§f Insulators: §e1×§f Bakelite Bar yields §e8×§f Insulators in a crafting table. Essential for circuits.
§b•§f Industrial Boiler: Required in the anvil recipe.

There is also a lab glassware method using Hazardous Material Tanks, but the Chemical Plant is faster.

§ePS:§f Once your cracked oil line produces Aromatic Hydrocarbons and Petroleum Gas, run a dedicated Chemical Plant for bakelite. It solves your plastic needs!
